div.head: I Em 3
div.ab: Gif hwa Cristenes mannes blód ageote, ne cume he na on ðæs cyninges neawiste, ær he on dædbote ga, swa him biscop tæce ⁊ his scrift him wisige.
Gif hwa Cristenes mannes blod ageote, ne cume he na on ðas cyninges ánsyne, ær he on dædbote ga, swa biscop him tæce ⁊ his scrift him wissige.
Gyf hwa Cristenes mannes blod ageote, ne cume he na on ðæs cyniges neawæste, gyf he cyninges man sy, ær he on dædbote ga, swa biscop him tæce ⁊ his scrift him wisige.
Si quis sceleratis manibus effundat sanguinem Christianum, non appareat in conspectu regis, priusquam emendationem ineat, sicut episcopus docebit et penitentia consulat.
[Be monslihte.] Gif hwa Cristenes mannes blód ageote, ne cume he na on ðæs cyninges neawiste, ær he on dædbote ga, swa him biscop tæce ⁊ his scrift him wisige.
Gif hwa Cristenes mannes blod ageote, ne cume he na on ðæs cyninges neawiste ær he on dædbote ga, swa him biscop tæce and his scrift him wisige.

(Über Todtschlag. Ld) Wenn jemand das Blut eines Christenmenschen vergiesst, komme er nicht in des Königs Nähe (Angesicht H Qu., wenn er des Königs Vasall ist B), bevor er Kirchenbusse antrete, wie ihm der Bischof vorschreibt und sein Beichtvater anweist.

(Of homicide. Ld) If anyone sheds the blood of a Christian man, let him not come into the king's presence (sight, H Qu.; if he is the king's man, B) before he undertakes penance, as the bishop prescribes for him and his confessor directs him.
If anyone sheds the blood of a Christian man, he shall not come anywhere near the king until he proceeds to do penance, as the bishop appoints for him or his confessor directs him.
And if anyone sheds Christian blood, he may not come into the proximity of the king until he undertakes penance as the bishop instructs him and his confessor directs him.

Der König wiederholt dies von sich aus II 4, wo er aber auch die Erfüllung der weltlichen Busse und Strafe ausbedingt.—Gerade der in Blutrache Verfolgte mochte durch Erlangung von Königsschutz, später Handfrieden, sich gegen Ermordung durch die Sippe des Erschlagenen zu schützen suchen

The king repeats this on his own account in II 4, where, however, he also stipulates the payment of the secular compensation and fine.—It was precisely the man pursued in blood-feud who might seek to protect himself against being killed by the kindred of the slain man by obtaining the king's protection, later the hand-peace

‘Nähe’ scheint mir originaler, weil mit hired II 4 synonymer als ‘Angesicht’, denn neahwest bedeutet auch ‘Gesellschaft, Genossenschaft’ und geradezu Königs ‘Gefolge’; Toller 712 II. Auch spricht V Atr 29 = VI 36 von cynges neaweste im selben Zusammenhange. Der Schreiber hlq mag auf ‘Angesicht’ verfallen sein aus der Vulgata, wo so häufig facies vorkommt.—‘Nähe’ ist wahrscheinlich hier nicht (wie Allen meint Anc. laws 273, der für ihre Grenze die in Pax o. I 390 angegebene hält) bloss örtlich zu verstehen, sondern gesellschaftlich

‘Nearness’ seems to me more original, because it is more synonymous than ‘face’ with hired in II 4, for neahwest also means ‘company, fellowship’ and indeed the king's ‘retinue’; Toller 712 II. Moreover V Atr 29 = VI 36 speaks of cynges neaweste in the same context. The scribe of hlq may have hit upon ‘face’ from the Vulgate, where facies occurs so often.—‘Nearness’ is probably not to be understood here merely in a spatial sense (as Allen thinks, Anc. laws 273, who takes its limit to be that stated in Pax above I 390), but in a social sense

‘wenn’ hier nur gleich ‘welcher’, wie sehr oft umgekehrt das Relativ statt gif (s. d. Wb am Ende) steht. Der Zusatz in B, nicht original, aber wesentlich richtig, denkt zunächst an Königs Vassallen; gerade mächtige Höflinge mochten zuerst Staat und Kirche zu trotzen wagen; s. Gl Blutrache 15c. Die Tendenz des Gesetzes ist Schutz des Königs vor, sogar unbewusstem, Verkehr mit Exkommunizierten; s. d. 14: 10. Schon Childebert a. 596 gebot: excommunicatus . . de palatio nostro sit omnino extraneus; ed. Boretius Mon. Germ., Capit. p. 15c. 2

‘if’ here simply equals ‘who’, just as, very often, conversely the relative stands for gif (see that word in Wb, at the end). The addition in B, not original but essentially correct, thinks first of the king's vassals; it was precisely powerful courtiers who might be the first to dare to defy State and Church; see Gl Blutrache 15c. The purpose of the law is to protect the king from intercourse, even unwitting, with excommunicates; see that word 14: 10. As early as 596 Childebert ordered: excommunicatus . . de palatio nostro sit omnino extraneus; ed. Boretius Mon. Germ., Capit. p. 15c. 2
Nicht aus dem Worte, aber aus stetigem Zusammenhange (s. Wb) erhellt die kirchliche Beschränkung der Bed. von dædbot. Auch hier ist ja die bestimmende Macht geistlich
The ecclesiastical restriction of the meaning of dædbot is clear not from the word itself but from its constant context (see Wb). Here too, after all, the determining authority is spiritual

‘Und’ bedeutet ‘beziehungsweise, oder’ (vgl. Gl Geistliches Gericht 3); bei Schwere des Falles oder Höhe des Missetäters bestimmt die Pönitenz (s. d. Gt 2. a) der Bischof, sonst der Pfarrer. Vielleicht um der Schwierigkeit wörtlicher Übersetzung zu entgehen, wählte Q für scrift die andere abstrakte Bed., etwa im Sinne von ‘Poenitentiale’, wie canon tæce EGu 3. Allein laut his ist scrift als Person zu verstehen

‘And’ means ‘or, as the case may be’ (cf. Gl Geistliches Gericht 3); where the case is grave or the offender of high rank the bishop determines the penance (see that word in Gt 2. a), otherwise the parish priest. Perhaps to avoid the difficulty of a literal translation, Q chose for scrift the other, abstract meaning, roughly in the sense of ‘penitential’, as in canon tæce EGu 3. But because of his, scrift is to be understood as a person
Q adds sceleratis manibus.
Liebermann prefers neawiste (D, B, cf. V Atr. 29; VI, 36) to ansyne (H) in view of the use of the word hired in II Edm. 4 where this regulation is practically repeated.

Liebermann is of opinion that, although the phrase gyf he cyninges man sy (B) did not form part of the original text, it conveys the true interpretation of its meaning; that is to say, that the law was drawn up primarily with reference to the nobles in the king’s entourage.
This interpretation follows Liebermann (iii. p. 125) who points out that the personal action of the bishop might be due to the gravity of the offence or the high rank of the offender.
